2.text: several parties of Cossacks and service-men on the Anadyr. One party was

3.text: headed by Semen Deshnev and the inspecting service official (служилый

4.text: приказный человѣкъ)¹ Semen Motora. Another party was headed by Michael

5.text: Stadukhin, who had come from the Kolyma River. Stadukhin made attempts

6.text: to subjugate to himself all other parties, and to be the chief leader of the

7.text: public officials of Anadyr. The strife brought forth several reports, which

8.text: were presented to the Governor of Yakutsk.² All these reports are just as

9.text: interesting as the report of Michael Stadukhin concerning the Kolyma.

10.text: Thus one Theodore Vetoshka, in a report of 1655, says, “In the past

11.text: 157th year (1649) it became known on the Kolyma River — from the lips

12.text: of Angara, the hostage of the Khodyntzy,³ whom we, your slaves [the report

13.text: is formulated as a direct address to the Czar], took on the upper stream of

14.text: the Anui River, and from other captives in the same raid of ours — that a

15.text: new trans-mountain river, the Anadyr,⁴ comes quite near to the upper course

16.text: of the Anui. By reason of these facts we have gathered together among

17.text: ourselves volunteer hunters, and we have struck the ground (i. e., petitioned)

18.text: before you, O Czar! because we desired to go to that new country with the

19.text: intention of bringing down the tributeless tribes under your high hand, and

20.text: we had to give into your treasury forty sables. Then we were given leave

21.text: to undertake that service, together with the public officials Semen Motora

22.text: and comrades.... And in the same 157th year, in the month of July, the

23.text: service-men Michael Stadukhin and comrades made an attempt to go by sea

24.text: from the Kolyma River to the new river Pahycha,⁵ but came back from the

25.text: sea to the Kolyma on Sept. 7. When we came over the mountain to the

26.text: Anadyr River, and he (Michael Stadukhin) was going down the Anadyr and

27.text: passed by our camp, he sent to us, requesting that we come to him and ask

28.text: to be accepted into his regiment, and stating that if we did not consent, he

29.text: would order all of us to be exterminated. Then he took from us by force

30.text: the inspecting official Semen Motora, and put him into the stocks for nine

31.text: days, and extorted from him a paper promising to remain under his (Michael’s)

33.text: It seems that Michael Stadukhin could not accomplish his purpose. So

37.text: ⁴ In these oldest reports Kolyma is often called “Kovyma”, and Anadyr is called “Anandyr.”

38.text: ⁵ The name “Pahycha River” is repeated several times in the reports. The Pahycha River is said to be

39.text: rich in sables. Some recent scientists have suggested that this name may have referred to the Amur River,

40.text: which in reality, even up to the present, abounds in sables; but the natives of the Kolyma hardly knew any-

41.text: thing of the distant Amur. They had knowledge only of the nearest rivers, such as the Anadyr and the

42.text: Penshina. Of these rivers, the Anadyr is mentioned as being, even at that time, poor in sable. The next

43.text: large river is the Poqaˊč, which forms the northern boundary-line of the sable territory, and which even now,

44.text: when the sable is rapidly vanishing in the north, still has some of the darkest and most valuable sables. It

45.text: is quite probable that the natives of the Kolyma, when speaking of Pahycha, had in mind this Poqaˊč River;
